findings.finding: Step 1 assumes a `# mechanism-ok:` marker whose reason names no ticket will still pass `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check`. That is false. The ratchet now requires every marker's reason to open with a ticket id: an alias, a two-quad id or a four-quad id. Any marker without one is an error. The key is also not in the baseline, so it is `new` and is admitted only by a marker whose reason opens with a ticket id. The plan's own example reason would make --check, and so `make verify`, exit 1. Step 1 contradicts AC2 and AC4.

findings.suggested_fix: Drop the rule that the reason must not name a ticket and pick one of two paths. (a) Open the reason with the id of a ticket that is already closed, or one that will never be closed under this marker. It must not be bossy-impish-hoiho or this ticket, because naming this ticket would block its own close. Follow it with the permanent justification, for example `# mechanism-ok: config_key verify.plan_review_engine — <closed-ticket-id> permanent operator choice between two supported engines (ADR 0123)`, and update AC2 to match. (b) If a ticket-free permanent admission really is the goal, add a planned step to extend the grammar in sunset_markers.py/compare.py, with tests and an AGENTS.md update. That is a behaviour change, so it would need to come out of the "wording only" framing.

findings.finding: Step 1 calls for a `# mechanism-ok:` marker whose reason names no ticket. The repository's marker rules reject that. Every harvested marker reason must start with a ticket id: a four-quad id, a two-quad id, or a three-word alias (`_SUNSET_RE` in src/rebar/_commands/sunset_markers.py). `_marker_errors` in scripts/_mechanism_delta/compare.py reports 'names no sunset ticket' for any other reason and fails the check, and `_partition` refuses to admit the key. `config_key::verify.plan_review_engine` is missing from .github/mechanism-baseline.json, so it is `new` and needs a marker that admits it. The fallbacks are also blocked: AGENTS.md forbids hand-editing the baseline, and `drain_stale` cannot add keys. The proposed reason therefore makes `check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exit 1, which also breaks `make lint` and `make verify`.

findings.suggested_fix: Keep the marker rules unchanged. Create or name a long-lived ownership ticket, for example 'Maintain the selectable plan-review engine switch (ADR 0123)', that is meant to stay open as the owner of this permanent config key. Rewrite the marker as `# mechanism-ok: config_key verify.plan_review_engine — <owner-ticket-id> permanent operator choice between two supported engines (ADR 0123)`. Change step 1 and AC2 to say the reason starts with that owner ticket id, does not name bossy-impish-hoiho or this ticket, and cites ADR 0123. Have the ADR 0123 amendment say the marker names a standing owner ticket rather than a sunset task. Avoid alias-shaped prose that only passes the shape check.

findings.finding: The grep in the first acceptance criterion only covers `src`, `rebar.toml`, ADR 0123, `docs/config.md` and `docs/plan-review-gate.md`. Step 5 is open-ended ('for example'), and the close only succeeds if no `# mechanism-ok:` marker anywhere still names `bossy-impish-hoiho`. References in `tests/`, `scripts/`, other docs, the README or CHANGELOG, or a mechanism-delta baseline file would escape the check. They would only surface later, when the post-merge close is refused. The criterion also relies on reviewer judgment ('no line about the engine switch') rather than a deterministic empty result.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria, first bullet (git grep scope); Plan step 5
